import html # Example template; in real usage this should be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

By {writer_name}

{body}
{tags}
""" def generate_post_html(writer_name: str, title: str, body: str, tag_list: list[str]) -> str: """ Construct a safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- writer_name : str Name of the author. title : str Post headline. body : str Main content of the post. tag_list : list[str] Tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str XSS‑protected HTML string formatted according to USER_POST_FORMAT. """ # Escape all user-provided content to prevent XSS safe_writer_name = html.escape(writer_name, quote=True) safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) # For the body we preserve line breaks but still escape HTML safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Build tags markup safe_tags = "".join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in tag_list ) # Format the final HTML return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( writer_name=safe_writer_name, title=safe_title, body=safe_body, tags=safe_tags )
